parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Dilip, husband; Smt Shakuntla, wife; Jai Singh, father-in-law; Yogesh, son-in-law; Smt Mamta, daughter-in-law; Smt Jyoti, daughter

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Ruby filed a complaint under section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005. She claimed domestic violence by Dilip and his family members. The trial court granted various reliefs to Ruby, including protection order, rent in lieu of alternate accommodation, monetary relief, and compensation order.

legal_principles.principle: Each and every case is to be decided on its merit after affording ample opportunities to the parties.
legal_principles.held: it is settled law that each and every case is to be decided on its merit after affording ample opportunities to the parties;
cited_cases: Dilip vs Smt. Ruby, (2021) X SCC Y

legal_principles.principle: Non-appearance of parties was neither willful nor intentional.
legal_principles.held: non-appearance of appellants was neither willful nor intentional.

outcome.final_order: The instant appeal filed by the appellants challenging the ex parte judgment dated 24.11.2018 was disposed of vide this judgment.
